# "The Lake of Fire: The Unending Judgment of Almighty God"

## A Sermon on Revelation 20:15

---

*"And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire."*

---

I want to speak to you plainly this hour, without apology, without evasion, and without the cowardice that has silenced too many pulpits in this generation. I will not give you poetry when Scripture gives you geography. I will not hand you sentiment when the Holy Spirit delivers verdict. What I am about to describe to you is not a parable. It is not symbolic language reaching for something milder. It is the destination — the actual, real, conscious, physical, eternal destination — of every human being whose name is not inscribed in the Lamb's Book of Life.

## I. The Place Is Real

The Lake of Fire is a location. It is as real as the ground beneath your feet this morning. More real, in fact, because the ground beneath your feet will one day be dissolved. Peter tells us that the elements themselves will melt with fervent heat. This earth you stand on is temporary. The Lake of Fire is not.

God prepared it. Jesus Christ Himself spoke of it. In Matthew 25:41, He called it "everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels." It was constructed by the hand of the same God who measured the heavens with a span. The same voice that said, "Let there be light" also ordained this place of unending fire. It exists now. It waits now. And at the final judgment, it receives its inhabitants — forever.

This is not the grave. This is not cessation. This is not a moment of discomfort followed by non-existence. Annihilation is a lie that men invented because they cannot bear the truth that God revealed. The Lake of Fire burns. It burns with literal fire. It burns with actual brimstone. And it never stops burning.

## II. The Duration Is Endless

I need you to hear me carefully, because this is where the human mind begins to retreat, and I will not allow you the comfort of retreat this morning.

Revelation 20:10 says the devil, the beast, and the false prophet "shall be tormented day and night for ever and ever." The phrase in the original language is *eis tous aionas ton aionon* — unto the ages of the ages. It is the strongest expression of unending duration that the Greek language is capable of producing. It is the same phrase used to describe the eternal life of God Himself in Revelation 4:10. If the Lake of Fire has an end, then God has an end. They stand or fall together. And God does not fall.

There is no conclusion. There is no final moment when the suffering ceases. There is no millionth year where mercy arrives. There is no reprieve. There is no parole. There is no court of appeals beyond the Great White Throne. When a soul enters the Lake of Fire, that soul has entered its eternal state. One billion years into that sentence, it has not begun. Ten billion years in, it is no closer to ending than the first second was. The word *forever* means what it has always meant, and no amount of theological manipulation can strip it of its meaning.

Jesus Himself said in Mark 9:48 that it is the place "where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched." He did not say the fire diminishes. He did not say the fire accomplishes its purpose and is then extinguished. He said it is **not quenched.** It burns and it burns and it burns, and no power in the created order puts it out, because the uncreated God sustains it as an everlasting monument to His justice.

## III. The Inhabitants Are Conscious

The rich man in Luke 16 was conscious. He could see. He could speak. He could feel. He could remember. He could reason. He could regret. And he could not escape.

Those who are cast into the Lake of Fire are not destroyed. They are sentenced. They are not eliminated from existence. They exist — fully, totally, consciously — in agony that does not relent. They will possess every faculty necessary to experience the full, undiminished weight of the wrath of Almighty God poured out without mixture. Revelation 14:10 says they will be tormented "with fire and brimstone in the presence of the holy angels, and in the presence of the Lamb." The Lamb will be there. Christ Himself will be the witness of that justice, because it is *His* justice. It is the justice that His cross satisfied for all who believed, and it is the justice that falls unrestrained upon all who did not.

There will be weeping. There will be gnashing of teeth. There will be screaming that never produces hoarseness, because the body given in the resurrection of the unjust is a body suited for eternal endurance of eternal punishment. You will not burn up. You will burn. There is a difference that should terrify every soul in this room who has not fled to Christ.

## IV. The Standard Is the Book of Life

Look again at the text: *"And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire."*

"Whosoever." That word makes no exceptions. It does not say "whosoever was exceedingly wicked." It does not say "whosoever was a murderer or an abuser of mankind." It says **whosoever.** The moral man whose name is not in that book will burn alongside the immoral man whose name is not in that book. The religious man who trusted in his religion rather than in the finished work of Jesus Christ will open his eyes in the same fire as the man who never once entered a house of worship. The standard is not your decency. The standard is not your sincerity. The standard is not your comparison to your neighbor. The standard is one thing and one thing only: **Is your name written in the Book of Life?**

And your name is written there by one means alone — the blood of Jesus Christ, received by faith, through repentance and surrender to Him as Lord.

## V. The Urgency Is Now

This is why we preach the Gospel. This is why we plead. This is why Paul said he persuaded men with *terror.* This is why we do not apologize for raising our voices and warning you with everything in us.

You are one heartbeat from eternity. One car accident. One blood clot. One stray bullet. One diagnosis. And if your name is not written in that Book when your eyes close for the last time on this earth, you will open them in a place of fire that has no exit, no end, no relief, and no hope. **Hope does not exist there.** That is perhaps the most terrifying reality of all. In this life, in this room, in this moment — hope exists. The cross stands. The blood of Christ is sufficient. The arms of the Savior are open. The invitation is genuine. "Whosoever will, let him come."

But there is a last moment for that invitation. And you do not know when it is.

---

Do not leave this place today without settling the matter of your eternity. Do not gamble your everlasting soul on the chance that you will have tomorrow, because tomorrow is not promised to you. What is promised to you is this: the Lake of Fire is real, it is eternal, and it is the destination of every soul outside of Christ.

Come to Him. Come to Him now. Come while the door is open, because the day is coming when it will be shut, and no man will open it.

*"He that hath ears to hear, let him hear."*

---

**Amen.**

# Teaching for Parents: Understanding Total Depravity and Your Children

## A Foundational Doctrine for Faithful Parenting

---

## Introduction

One of the most important — and most countercultural — truths that will shape your parenting is the biblical doctrine known as **Total Depravity**. This teaching, drawn from Scripture and affirmed throughout church history, addresses the fundamental spiritual condition of every human being, including your children.

Understanding this doctrine is not meant to make you look at your children with despair. Quite the opposite — it is meant to drive you to the Gospel with urgency and to parent with eternal perspective. When we rightly understand the problem, we rightly value the solution.

---

## Part 1: What Is Total Depravity?

Total Depravity does not mean that every person is as evil as they could possibly be. Rather, it teaches that **every part of the human person — mind, will, emotions, body — has been affected and corrupted by sin.** There is no neutral ground in the human heart. No faculty has been left untouched by the Fall.

This doctrine rests on the biblical teaching that when Adam sinned, he did not sin as a private individual. He sinned as the **federal head** — the representative — of the entire human race. His guilt and his corrupted nature have been passed down to every one of his descendants.

> "Therefore, just as sin came into the world through one man, and death through sin, and so death spread to all men because all sinned…" — **Romans 5:12**

> "Behold, I was brought forth in iniquity, and in sin did my mother conceive me." — **Psalm 51:5**

> "The LORD saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every intention of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually." — **Genesis 6:5**

> "Among whom we all once lived in the passions of our flesh, carrying out the desires of the body and the mind, and were by nature children of wrath, like the rest of mankind." — **Ephesians 2:3**

---

## Part 2: Your Children Are Not Born "Innocent"

This is perhaps the hardest truth for parents to accept. Our culture — and even much of the visible church — promotes the idea that children are born as blank slates, morally neutral, essentially good, and only corrupted later by their environment. **This is not the biblical picture.**

Scripture teaches that your children enter the world with a **fallen nature inherited from Adam.** They are not born morally neutral. They are born with a nature that is bent toward sin, rebellion, and self-worship. David did not say, "I was brought forth in innocence." He said, "I was brought forth in **iniquity**" (Psalm 51:5).

Paul, writing under the inspiration of the Holy Spirit, described the natural condition of every human being — not just adults — when he said we are **"by nature children of wrath, like the rest of mankind"** (Ephesians 2:3). Notice: this is not something we become; it is something we are **by nature**, from the very beginning.

This means:

- **Your newborn is not morally innocent before God.** They bear Adam's guilt and Adam's corruption.
- **Your toddler does not need to be taught to sin.** They sin because it flows naturally from their fallen heart. You never have to teach a child to lie, to be selfish, to rage, or to defy authority. These things emerge organically because of what they are by nature.
- **Your children are born as slaves to sin.** Jesus Himself taught, "Truly, truly, I say to you, everyone who practices sin is a slave to sin" (John 8:34). Paul wrote that we were once "slaves of sin" (Romans 6:17, 20). This bondage is not something that develops over time — it is the default condition of the unregenerate heart from conception.

This does not mean your children are unlovable. It does not mean they are monsters. It means they are **fallen image-bearers** who desperately need what only God can give.

---

## Part 3: Even Their "Good" Behavior Is Stained

Here is where the doctrine becomes even more searching. Parents naturally delight when their children share, obey, show kindness, or say "please" and "thank you." And outwardly, these behaviors are certainly preferable to their opposites. **But we must be careful not to confuse outward conformity with inward righteousness.**

Scripture teaches:

> "All our righteous deeds are like a polluted garment." — **Isaiah 64:6**

> "Whatever does not proceed from faith is sin." — **Romans 14:23**

The standard of true goodness before God is not merely external compliance. It is **action that flows from a heart of faith, motivated by love for God, and directed toward His glory.** A child who shares a toy because they fear punishment, desire praise, or simply follow social conditioning is not performing a spiritually "good" act in the way Scripture defines goodness. The act may be **civilly good** — beneficial to society, commendable in the eyes of men — but it is not **savingly good** before a holy God.

This is not a minor distinction. The Pharisees were externally exemplary. They tithed, prayed, fasted, and kept the law with meticulous care. And yet Jesus called them whitewashed tombs — beautiful on the outside, full of death within (Matthew 23:27). The problem was never primarily their **behavior** but their **hearts**.

The same principle applies to your children. Without the regenerating work of the Holy Spirit, even their best moments are performed by hearts that do not love God supremely, do not act from faith, and are curved inward upon themselves. This does not mean we should not train them in right behavior — **we absolutely should** — but we must never confuse behavioral training with spiritual transformation.

Total depravity means the stain of sin reaches into **every** deed, **every** thought, **every** motive. There is no pocket of purity in the unregenerate heart that produces truly God-honoring fruit.

---

## Part 4: Under the Same Judgment from Birth

This is a solemn truth, but it is one that faithful parents must face: **without supernatural intervention, your children stand under the same divine judgment as the rest of fallen humanity from the moment of their birth.**

Paul's argument in Romans is sweeping and without exception:

> "None is righteous, no, not one; no one understands; no one seeks for God. All have turned aside; together they have become worthless; no one does good, not even one." — **Romans 3:10-12**

> "For the wages of sin is death…" — **Romans 6:23**

> "For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God." — **Romans 3:23**

The phrase "not even one" leaves no room for an age-based exception. The universal scope of sin and condemnation encompasses every descendant of Adam. Your children are included.

This does not mean we cannot have hope — we will come to that — but it does mean we must be **honest** about their condition. If we soften the diagnosis, we will inevitably soften the cure. If we tell ourselves that our children are basically good and just need guidance, we will parent as moralists rather than as Gospel-driven mothers and fathers. We will aim for behavior modification rather than heart transformation. And we will raise children who think they can earn God's favor rather than children who know they desperately need His grace.

---

## Part 5: Why This Doctrine Should Transform Your Parenting

If you truly believe this doctrine, it will revolutionize the way you raise your children. Here is how:

### 1. You Will Pray with Greater Urgency

If your children's greatest need were education, you would educate them. If their greatest need were self-esteem, you would affirm them. But if their greatest need is **regeneration** — a supernatural act of God that gives them a new heart — then your greatest parenting tool is **prayer.** You will plead with God to do what no parenting technique, no curriculum, no moral instruction can accomplish: to raise your children from spiritual death to spiritual life (Ephesians 2:4-5).

### 2. You Will Point Beyond Behavior to the Heart

You will not be satisfied with mere outward obedience. When you correct your children, you will probe their hearts. Why did they disobey? What were they worshipping in that moment? What idol were they serving? You will use every act of discipline as an opportunity to show them their need for a Savior who can change them **from the inside out.**

### 3. You Will Preach the Gospel to Them Constantly

If your children are dead in trespasses and sins (Ephesians 2:1), they do not need a pep talk. They need the Gospel — the good news that Christ died for sinners, that He lived the righteous life they could never live, that He bore the wrath they deserve, and that He offers free grace to all who repent and believe. You will never tire of telling them this story because you know it is the **only** power that can save them (Romans 1:16).

### 4. You Will Rely on the Holy Spirit, Not Your Own Efforts

This doctrine humbles parents. You cannot regenerate your children. You cannot argue them into the kingdom. You cannot behaviorally condition them into a new nature. You are utterly dependent on God to do the decisive work. This drives you to your knees and keeps you there.

### 5. You Will Marvel at Grace

When you understand the depths of your children's fallenness — and your own — you will marvel all the more at the grace of God. The doctrine of Total Depravity is not ultimately a doctrine of despair. It is the **dark backdrop** against which the diamond of the Gospel shines most brilliantly. The worse the disease, the more glorious the cure.

---

## Part 6: But What About God's Mercy?

Some parents may ask: "Does this mean my child is hopeless?" **Absolutely not.** But their hope is not found in themselves — it is found entirely in God.

> "But God, being rich in mercy, because of the great love with which he loved us, even when we were dead in our trespasses, made us alive together with Christ — by grace you have been saved." — **Ephesians 2:4-5**

The very passage that calls us "children of wrath" also declares the triumph of God's mercy. The same chapter that describes our spiritual death announces our spiritual resurrection in Christ. This is the breathtaking movement of the Gospel: from death to life, from wrath to mercy, from slavery to freedom.

And this is precisely why the doctrine of Total Depravity is not the enemy of hope — it is the **foundation** of hope. Because when we know that salvation is entirely the work of God, we know that **nothing** is too hard for Him. He specializes in raising the dead. He delights in saving the helpless. He calls things that are not as though they were (Romans 4:17).

Your children's only hope — like yours, like mine — is the sovereign, effectual, irresistible grace of God working through the Gospel of Jesus Christ.

---

## Part 7: A Word About Infant Death and God's Character

Many parents, upon hearing this doctrine, immediately ask about children who die in infancy. This is a tender and important question, and while Scripture does not give us an explicit, comprehensive answer, we can affirm several things:

1. **God is just.** He will never do wrong (Genesis 18:25).
2. **God is merciful.** He delights in showing mercy (Micah 7:18).
3. **God is sovereign over salvation.** He is able to apply the benefits of Christ's work to whomever He chooses, in whatever way He chooses, at whatever time He chooses.
4. **Many Reformed theologians** have affirmed a confident hope that God, in His mercy, applies the saving work of Christ to elect infants who die before they are able to profess faith. This does not contradict Total Depravity — it confirms it, because even in such cases, the child would be saved not by innocence but by **grace.**

We entrust these mysteries to the character of God and rest in His goodness.

---

## Conclusion: Parent as One Who Knows the Truth

Dear parents, your children are precious gifts from God. They are made in His image. They are worthy of your sacrificial love, your tireless care, and your deepest affection. **But they are not innocent.** They are born as children of wrath, slaves to sin, bearing the corruption of Adam, and standing in desperate need of the saving work of Jesus Christ.

This is not harsh. This is **honest.** And only honest theology produces faithful parenting.

Do not soften this truth. Do not sentimentalize childhood. Do not assume that your children's cuteness is evidence of their righteousness. Instead, love them enough to tell them the truth: they are sinners who need a Savior. And then point them — relentlessly, joyfully, and with tears if necessary — to the only One who can deliver them from the dominion of darkness and transfer them into the kingdom of His beloved Son (Colossians 1:13).

Pray for them. Plead with God on their behalf. Saturate your home with the Gospel. Model repentance and faith before them every day. And trust that the God who commands you to raise them in the nurture and admonition of the Lord (Ephesians 6:4) is the same God who is mighty to save.

> "And I am sure of this, that he who began a good work in you will bring it to completion at the day of Jesus Christ." — **Philippians 1:6**

---

*Soli Deo Gloria*

---

### Recommended Further Reading:
- *Original Sin* by Jonathan Edwards
- *The Doctrine of Sin* by Herman Bavinck (Reformed Dogmatics, Vol. 3)
- *Shepherding a Child's Heart* by Tedd Tripp
- *What Every Parent Needs to Know* by Paul David Tripp
- *The Westminster Confession of Faith*, Chapter VI: "Of the Fall of Man, of Sin, and of the Punishment Thereof"

# 2 Thessalonians 1:9 — An Explanation

## The Text

> "They will suffer the punishment of eternal destruction, away from the presence of the Lord and from the glory of his might" (ESV)

In Japanese translations, this is often rendered with phrases like **「永遠の滅び」(eien no horobi)**.

## Understanding "Eternal Destruction" (ὄλεθρον αἰώνιον)

### What the phrase means contextually

Paul is writing to the Thessalonian church about the return of Christ and the final judgment. Several key elements deserve attention:

**1. "Destruction" (ὄλεθρος / olethros)**
This Greek word does not mean annihilation or ceasing to exist. Paul uses this word elsewhere (1 Corinthians 5:5; 1 Timothy 6:9) to describe ruin and devastating loss — the loss of everything good, meaningful, and blessed. It conveys the idea of **complete ruin**, not non-existence.

**2. "Eternal" (αἰώνιος / aiōnios)**
This is the same word used for "eternal life" (ζωὴν αἰώνιον). If eternal life is unending, the same adjective applied to destruction indicates an unending state. The destruction is not a momentary event but an **ongoing, permanent condition**.

**3. "Away from the presence of the Lord"**
This is perhaps the most devastating dimension. The punishment is described fundamentally as **separation from God's presence and glory**. Since God is the source of all goodness, beauty, truth, joy, love, and life, to be separated from Him is to be separated from everything that makes existence bearable or meaningful.

### Theological summary

Eternal destruction involves:

- **Permanent exclusion** from God's gracious presence
- **Irreversible ruin** — not temporary correction, but a final state
- **Conscious experience** — it is described as "punishment" (δίκην), which implies awareness
- **Just retribution** — verse 8 specifies it comes upon "those who do not know God and do not obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus"

## Regarding the Japanese People Specifically

It is important to clarify several things:

### What Scripture affirms universally

The Bible does not single out any ethnicity for condemnation. The condition described in this passage applies to **all people everywhere** — Japanese, American, African, European — who "do not know God and do not obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ" (v. 8). This is a universal human problem:

- "All have sinned and fall short of the glory of God" (Romans 3:23)
- "There is no distinction" between peoples (Romans 3:22)

### The urgency for Japan

Japan is often described as one of the largest unreached nations, with Christians comprising roughly 1–2% of the population. This creates a profound **missionary urgency**, not a reason for condemnation or dismissal. Several considerations arise:

**1. God's heart for the Japanese people**
God "desires all people to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth" (1 Timothy 2:4). This includes every Japanese person. God is "not wishing that any should perish, but that all should reach repentance" (2 Peter 3:9).

**2. The question of those who haven't heard**
Romans 1:18–20 teaches that all people have some knowledge of God through creation and conscience (Romans 2:14–15). However, Scripture also places responsibility on the church to proclaim the gospel: "How are they to believe in him of whom they have never heard? And how are they to hear without someone preaching?" (Romans 10:14).

This passage should stir Christians toward:
- **Compassion**, not superiority
- **Prayer** for Japan
- **Missionary commitment** to ensure the gospel is clearly and lovingly presented
- **Humility**, recognizing that apart from grace, every person faces the same judgment

**3. God is the just Judge**
Abraham's question remains foundational: "Shall not the Judge of all the earth do what is just?" (Genesis 18:25). God's judgment is perfectly righteous, fully informed, and takes into account what each person has received and known. We can trust His justice while urgently sharing His mercy.

## Conclusion

2 Thessalonians 1:9 is a sobering text that describes the ultimate consequence of rejecting or remaining apart from God — an eternal, irreversible separation from His presence that constitutes complete ruin. This reality applies to all unbelieving people regardless of nationality. For the Japanese context, where so many have not yet clearly heard the gospel, this passage should be understood not as a verdict already sealed but as a **call to the church** to bring the message of salvation with urgency, love, and cultural sensitivity — because God's desire is that people from every nation, including Japan, would be saved.

> "After this I looked, and behold, a great multitude that no one could number, **from every nation**, from all tribes and peoples and languages, standing before the throne..." — Revelation 7:9

# The Condition of the Natural Man

---

**Opening Scripture Reading:**

*"The wicked are estranged from the womb: they go astray as soon as they be born, speaking lies."* — Psalm 58:3

*"Among whom also we all had our conversation in times past in the lusts of our flesh, fulfilling the desires of the flesh and of the mind; and were by nature the children of wrath, even as others."* — Ephesians 2:3

---

## Introduction

Beloved, I come to you this day with a subject that the modern world despises, that the carnal ear refuses to hear, and that the natural heart recoils against with every fiber of its being. And yet it is a subject without which no man, no woman, no soul walking upon this earth can rightly understand the Gospel, the Cross, or the mercy of Almighty God.

I speak to you concerning **the condition of the natural man** — the state of every son and daughter of Adam who has not been born again by the sovereign, regenerating work of the Holy Spirit.

And I must say plainly at the outset: what I am about to declare is not my opinion. It is not the invention of any theologian, council, or denomination. It is the plain, unvarnished, uncompromising testimony of Holy Scripture — the very Word of the living God — and it will stand when heaven and earth have passed away.

---

### I. The World's Diagnosis vs. God's Diagnosis

We live in an age that has perfected the art of flattering the human soul. The world will tell a man that he is "basically good." It will tell him he is "imperfect" — as though **Sin** were merely a cosmetic blemish, a scratch upon an otherwise beautiful portrait. Modern religion — and I grieve to say it — has largely adopted this same spirit. It speaks of man as "flawed," as "broken," as someone who simply needs a little help, a little encouragement, a little moral improvement.

But beloved, **that is not what the Bible says.**

The Bible does not say man is imperfect. The Bible says man is **dead.**

*"And you hath he quickened, who were dead in trespasses and sins."* — Ephesians 2:1

Not wounded. Not weakened. Not stumbling. **Dead.** Dead in trespasses and in **Sin.** A corpse has no ability to revive itself. A corpse does not cooperate with life. A corpse does not "decide" to breathe again. And this is God's own portrait of the natural man — not a patient in need of medicine, but a cadaver in need of resurrection.

---

### II. Sin — Not a Deficiency, but a Dominion

Let us understand what **Sin** truly is in the life of the unregenerate soul. Sin is not merely what a man *does*; it is what a man *is.* It is not an occasional failure; it is a reigning monarch upon the throne of the human heart.

*"The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked: who can know it?"* — Jeremiah 17:9

Every faculty of the natural man is saturated with **Sin.** His mind is darkened — *"the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him"* (1 Corinthians 2:14). His will is enslaved — *"ye were the servants of sin"* (Romans 6:17). His affections are disordered — he loves what God hates and hates what God loves. His righteousness, his very best deeds, the noblest works of his hands, are — hear it from the prophet Isaiah — *"as filthy rags"* (Isaiah 64:6).

**Sin** has not merely touched the natural man. It has *totalized* him. There is no island of goodness within him to which God may appeal. There is no untouched corner of his soul where a spark of spiritual life flickers, waiting to be fanned into flame. He is, from the crown of his head to the sole of his foot, under the dominion and pollution of **Sin.**

---

### III. Enmity — The True Posture of the Natural Heart

But now we must go further, and here the truth becomes still more dreadful. The natural man is not merely corrupted by **Sin** — he stands in active, personal **Enmity** against the living God.

Hear the Apostle Paul:

*"Because the carnal mind is enmity against God: for it is not subject to the law of God, neither indeed can be."* — Romans 8:7

Mark that carefully. Paul does not say the carnal mind is *at* enmity — as though it were a temporary quarrel that might be resolved by negotiation. He says the carnal mind **is Enmity.** The hostility is not incidental to the natural man's character — it is *essential* to it. **Enmity** against God is woven into the very fabric of fallen human nature.

This means, beloved — and I say it with the utmost solemnity — that every person who has not been born again is not merely distant from God, not merely indifferent to God, but is a **literal enemy of God.**

*"The friendship of the world is enmity with God. Whosoever therefore will be a friend of the world is the enemy of God."* — James 4:4

And again Paul writes to the Colossians, reminding those who had been saved of what they *once were*:

*"And you, that were sometime alienated and enemies in your mind by wicked works..."* — Colossians 1:21

**Enemies.** Not merely strangers. Not merely wanderers. **Enemies.** And this **Enmity** is not passive — it is a living, active, continual rebellion against the authority, the law, the holiness, and the very Person of God. The natural man may dress it in the garments of morality, culture, philosophy, and even religion — but underneath every stitch is the same ancient **Enmity** that first raised its head in the Garden of Eden when our father Adam chose his own will over the command of his Maker.

---

### IV. Condemned Already — Not Waiting for Judgment, but Under It

And now, beloved, we come to a point that should make every unconverted soul in this room tremble. The natural man is not merely in danger of future condemnation. He is not merely "at risk." He is — in the words of the Lord Jesus Christ Himself — **condemned already.**

*"He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God."* — John 3:18

**Already.** The gavel has fallen. The sentence has been pronounced. The verdict is rendered. The natural man walks about this earth — eating, drinking, laughing, planning, building — all the while carrying upon his soul the sentence of eternal condemnation. He does not need to wait for the Great White Throne to learn his standing before God. His standing is **Enmity.** His condition is **Sin.** His sentence is condemnation. And it is *already* in effect.

*"He that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abideth on him."* — John 3:36

The wrath of God does not merely *await* the unbeliever. It **abides** on him. It rests upon him at this very hour. It hovers over him like a storm cloud that has not yet broken, but is charged with the full fury of divine justice. Every breath the natural man takes, he takes under the forbearance of a God whom he has offended. Every heartbeat is an undeserved mercy granted to an **enemy of God** who deserves nothing but wrath.

---

### V. A Provocation to the Wrath of God

And this brings us, finally, to the most sobering reality of all. The very *nature* of the natural man — not merely his worst deeds, but his **nature**, his existence as an unregenerate creature steeped in **Sin** and governed by **Enmity** — is a continual provocation to the wrath of a holy God.

God is not merely displeased with what sinners do. God is opposed to what sinners **are.** A holy God cannot look upon **Sin** with the slightest degree of allowance. His holiness is not a passive attribute; it is a consuming fire.

*"For our God is a consuming fire."* — Hebrews 12:29

*"God is angry with the wicked every day."* — Psalm 7:11

**Every day.** Not occasionally. Not when the sinner commits some extraordinary act of wickedness. **Every day.** The natural man's entire existence — his thoughts, his motives, his ambitions, his pleasures, his religion without regeneration — all of it is a rising vapor of provocation before the nostrils of a righteous God. His **Sin** is not a private matter between himself and his conscience; it is a public affront to the majesty of the King of heaven. His **Enmity** is not hidden from the eyes of the Almighty — it is open, naked, and fully exposed before Him with whom we have to do.

And yet — and here is the wonder — **that God has not already consumed us all.**

---

### A Word Before We Proceed

Now, beloved, I know that what I have said thus far is hard. It is sharp. It cuts against every instinct of the natural mind. The flesh hears these truths and cries out, "Unfair! Unjust! Too harsh!"

But I say to you: it is only against this dark canvas — this terrible, honest portrait of human **Sin**, human **Enmity**, human condemnation, and the just wrath of God — that the Gospel shines in its true and magnificent glory.

If man is only imperfect, he needs only improvement.
If man is only lost, he needs only direction.
If man is only sick, he needs only medicine.

**But if man is dead, condemned, and an enemy of God by nature — then he needs nothing less than a Savior who can raise the dead, justify the ungodly, and reconcile enemies to God by the blood of His Cross.**

And **that**, beloved, is precisely what we have in the Lord Jesus Christ.

But before we come to the remedy, we must sit for a moment longer with the disease. For no man will ever flee to Christ who does not first understand what he is fleeing *from.*

# Joshua 11:20 — The Hardening of the Canaanites and the Sovereignty of God in Judgment

> *"For it was of the LORD to harden their hearts, that they should come against Israel in battle, that he might destroy them utterly, and that they might have no favour, but that he might destroy them, as the LORD commanded Moses."* — Joshua 11:20 (KJV)

---

## Introduction: A Text That Demands Reverence, Not Revision

This verse stands as one of the most sobering declarations in all of Scripture. It pulls back the veil on the hidden counsel of God and reveals a divine purpose operating behind the military campaigns of Joshua: **God Himself hardened the hearts of the Canaanite nations so that they would march headlong into battle, receive no mercy, and be utterly destroyed.**

Modern sentimentality recoils at this. The natural man finds it offensive. But the student of Scripture must approach this text not as a judge over God but as a creature standing before his Creator, seeking to understand what the LORD has been pleased to reveal about Himself. We do not come to soften this verse. We come to sit under it, to learn from it, and to worship the God it reveals.

---

## I. The Historical Context: What Was Happening

By Joshua 11, Israel has swept through the southern campaign. Now a massive northern coalition, led by Jabin king of Hazor, gathers an army described as numerous "as the sand that is upon the sea shore" (11:4). This was not a defensive posture. These kings *came out* to fight. They initiated aggression against Israel.

Verse 20 then provides the **theological explanation** behind their military aggression: it was *of the LORD* to harden their hearts. The Hebrew is unambiguous. The word translated "harden" (חַזֵּק, *chazzeq*) means to strengthen, to make firm, to make resolute. God made their hearts firm in their hostility, firm in their rebellion, firm in their determination to fight rather than flee, submit, or seek terms of peace.

The purpose clause is threefold and devastating:

1. **"That they should come against Israel in battle"** — God ensured they would fight.
2. **"That he might destroy them utterly"** (*cherem* — devote to total destruction) — God ensured total judgment.
3. **"That they might have no favour"** (no mercy, no grace, no clemency) — God ensured no avenue of escape.

This was not an accident of war. This was the deliberate, purposeful, sovereign orchestration of Almighty God.

---

## II. God Has the Sovereign Right to Deny Mercy

The first truth that must be established and affirmed without equivocation is this: **God is under no obligation whatsoever to extend mercy to any sinner or any nation.**

Mercy, by its very nature, is *undeserved*. The moment mercy becomes obligatory, it ceases to be mercy and becomes a debt. Paul establishes this principle with crushing finality in Romans 9:

> *"Therefore hath he mercy on whom he will have mercy, and whom he will he hardeneth."* — Romans 9:18

> *"Nay but, O man, who art thou that repliest against God? Shall the thing formed say to him that formed it, Why hast thou made me thus? Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour?"* — Romans 9:20–21

Paul is not embarrassed by divine hardening. He appeals to it as a demonstration of God's absolute prerogative. And when he anticipates the objection — "Then why does God still find fault?" — he does not retreat into philosophical qualifications. He silences the objector: *"Who art thou that repliest against God?"*

### The Canaanites deserved judgment.

This point cannot be overstated. The Canaanites were not innocent bystanders. By the time of Joshua's conquest, the iniquity of the Amorites had been accumulating for over **four hundred years** (Genesis 15:16). God told Abraham that the conquest would be delayed precisely because their sin had not yet reached its fullness. That means God, in His patience, gave the Canaanite peoples four centuries of common grace — four centuries during which they plunged ever deeper into:

- **Child sacrifice** — burning their sons and daughters alive to Molech (Leviticus 18:21; Deuteronomy 12:31)
- **Sexual perversion of every kind** — incest, homosexuality, bestiality (Leviticus 18:6–23)
- **Occultism and demonism** — necromancy, divination, sorcery (Deuteronomy 18:9–12)
- **Systemic, culture-wide moral corruption** — so profound that God says the very *land* was defiled and vomited them out (Leviticus 18:25, 28)

These were not minor cultural differences. This was civilizational depravity of the most extreme order. The Canaanites did not sin in ignorance; they sinned against the light of conscience, the light of creation, and the testimony of God's dealings with the nations around them, including the witness of Israel's miraculous deliverance from Egypt, which Rahab herself acknowledged was known throughout the land (Joshua 2:9–11).

**Every single Canaanite deserved the wrath of God.** And here is the crucial point: *so does every single human being who has ever lived.* "The wages of sin is death" (Romans 6:23). "All have sinned and come short of the glory of God" (Romans 3:23). If God were to harden the hearts of every sinner on earth and destroy them all, He would commit no injustice. He would give them exactly what they have earned.

When God extends mercy, He acts according to His grace. When God withholds mercy and hardens, He acts according to His justice. **Neither action is unjust. Both glorify Him.**

---

## III. Why God Hardened Their Hearts: The Purposes of God in Ensuring Judgment Without Mercy

### A. To Execute the Fullness of His Justice

Partial judgment upon the Canaanites would have been inadequate. God had decreed *cherem* — total destruction, total devotion to His wrath. The sin of the Canaanites warranted nothing less than complete eradication. If their hearts had softened, if they had sued for peace merely out of self-preservation (as the Gibeonites did through deception in Joshua 9), the full measure of divine justice would not have been carried out.

God hardened their hearts so that justice would not be short-circuited by cowardice, pragmatism, or self-interested capitulation. **He ensured that the punishment fit the crime — fully, completely, and without remainder.**

This is the same principle we see in the eschatological judgments of Revelation. God does not relent in pouring out the bowls of wrath because the wicked do not relent in their sin. In fact, even under the outpouring of divine wrath, they "blasphemed the God of heaven because of their pains and their sores, and repented not of their deeds" (Revelation 16:11). The hardening continues because the judgment must be complete.

### B. To Display His Wrath and Make Known His Power

Paul articulates this purpose explicitly:

> *"What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction: and that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy, which he had afore prepared unto glory?"* — Romans 9:22–23

There is a divine "what if" here that Paul offers as entirely reasonable and right. God displays His attributes through both mercy and wrath. The full spectrum of His glory is revealed not only in salvation but in judgment. **A God who never judges is a God whose holiness is never vindicated, whose justice is never displayed, whose hatred of sin is never demonstrated.**

The destruction of the Canaanites was a **theater of divine justice** — a public, historical demonstration to Israel and to all nations that the God of Israel is holy, that He will not tolerate sin indefinitely, and that His patience has a terminus.

Without hardening, the Canaanites might have feigned repentance out of fear, as conquered peoples often do. They might have negotiated survival while retaining their idolatrous practices in their hearts. God foreclosed this possibility. **He ensured the demonstration would be pure, complete, and unmistakable.**

### C. To Protect Israel from Spiritual Contamination

God explicitly states the pastoral reason for total destruction:

> *"But thou shalt utterly destroy them... that they teach you not to do after all their abominations, which they have done unto their gods; so should ye sin against the LORD your God."* — Deuteronomy 20:17–18

And what happened when Israel failed to carry out complete destruction? Exactly what God warned. The remaining Canaanite populations drew Israel into idolatry, syncretism, and every form of moral degradation. The entire book of Judges is a testimony to the catastrophic consequences of incomplete obedience to the *cherem*.

God hardened the Canaanites' hearts so they would fight and be destroyed rather than survive and corrupt. **This hardening was an act of severe mercy toward Israel even as it was an act of judgment toward Canaan.**

### D. To Foreshadow the Final Judgment

The conquest of Canaan is typological. It points forward to the final, eschatological destruction of all who persist in rebellion against God. Just as the Canaanites were devoted to destruction with no quarter given, so the final judgment will be total, irreversible, and without mercy for those outside of Christ:

> *"Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels."* — Matthew 25:41

> *"And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire."* — Revelation 20:15

There is no plea bargain at the Great White Throne. There is no eleventh-hour mercy for those whom God has given over to their own wickedness. The hardening of the Canaanites was a historical preview of the principle that governs the final state: **those whom God does not save, He judges — completely and forever.**

---

## IV. In What Sense Is This 'Good'?

This is the question that disturbs the natural mind most deeply: How can it be *good* that God ensures some do not repent so that they are destroyed?

The answer lies in understanding what "good" means according to Scripture, not according to fallen human sentiment.

### A. It Is Good Because God's Holiness Demands It

God is infinitely holy. His holiness is not a passive attribute — it is active, burning, consuming. "Our God is a consuming fire" (Hebrews 12:29). Sin is an infinite offense against this infinite holiness. When sin reaches its fullness and God's patience reaches its appointed end, it is **morally right, fitting, and good** for that sin to be consumed.

If a human judge let a serial murderer go free because he felt compassion, we would not call it mercy — we would call it a miscarriage of justice. How much more when the crimes in question are committed against the infinitely glorious God? **The destruction of the impenitent is the satisfaction of divine justice, and the satisfaction of divine justice is a profoundly good thing.**

### B. It Is Good Because It Vindicates God's Truthfulness

God had promised judgment upon the Canaanites. He told Abraham it would come (Genesis 15:16). He told Moses to execute it (Deuteronomy 7:1–2). He told Joshua to carry it out (Joshua 1). If the Canaanites had somehow averted this judgment through pretended repentance or strategic submission, the word of God would have fallen to the ground. God's hardening of their hearts **ensured the integrity of His own word.**

> *"God is not a man, that he should lie; neither the son of man, that he should repent: hath he said, and shall he not do it? or hath he spoken, and shall he not make it good?"* — Numbers 23:19

### C. It Is Good Because It Magnifies Grace by Contrast

We cannot appreciate the height of mercy without understanding the depth of judgment. The riches of God's grace in salvation are magnified, intensified, and made glorious precisely against the backdrop of what sinners deserve and what some sinners receive.

Rahab the harlot was a Canaanite. She lived in Jericho. She practiced the same religion, breathed the same cultural air, participated in the same civilization. Yet God opened her heart to believe, and she was saved — brought into the covenant people, placed in the genealogy of the Messiah Himself (Matthew 1:5). **Every time we read of the Canaanites being destroyed, we should marvel that Rahab was spared.** That is the wonder of grace. And it shines brightest when we see what happens to those who do not receive it.

Romans 9:23 makes this explicit: God endures vessels of wrath *so that* He might make known the riches of His glory on vessels of mercy. **The destruction of the hardened Canaanites serves the glory of the mercy shown to Rahab and to every sinner who believes.**

### D. It Is Good Because God Defines Good

Ultimately, the deepest answer is this: **whatever God does is good because God is the standard of goodness.** He does not conform to an external standard of morality above Himself. He *is* the standard. His nature is the definition of good. His will is the expression of that nature.

> *"Shall not the Judge of all the earth do right?"* — Genesis 18:25

The answer is always, invariably, and necessarily **yes**. If God hardens hearts, it is right. If God withholds mercy, it is just. If God devotes nations to destruction, it is holy. Not because we can fully comprehend every dimension of His purpose, but because **He is God and we are not.**

---

## V. The Hardening of the Canaanites and the Hardening of Pharaoh: A Consistent Pattern

Joshua 11:20 is not an anomaly. It follows the same pattern established in the Exodus:

> *"And the LORD hardened the heart of Pharaoh, and he hearkened not unto them; as the LORD had spoken unto Moses."* — Exodus 9:12

In both cases:
- God hardened hearts that were already in rebellion
- God hardened hearts for the purpose of judgment
- God hardened hearts to display His own glory and power
- God hardened hearts so that His purposes would be accomplished fully

This is not divine cruelty. It is divine sovereignty acting upon sinners who are already guilty, already deserving of wrath, already in a state of moral corruption. **God does not harden innocent hearts. He hardens guilty ones. And in doing so, He ensures that they receive what they have chosen — rebellion — and what rebellion deserves — destruction.**

---

## VI. Addressing the Objection: "Doesn't This Make God Unjust?"

Paul anticipates this very objection and answers it with apostolic authority:

> *"Is there unrighteousness with God? God forbid."* — Romans 9:14

The objection assumes that God owes mercy to sinners. He does not. The objection assumes that sinners have a right not to be hardened. They do not. The objection assumes that human beings stand in a position to evaluate God's justice. They do not.

**God is the Creator. Man is the creature. God is the Potter. Man is the clay. God is the Judge. Man is the accused.**

When a convicted criminal stands before a judge, the criminal does not get to dictate the terms of sentencing. How infinitely more true when sinful creatures stand before the thrice-holy God who made them, sustains them, and against whom they have sinned.

Furthermore, we must understand that hardening is not the imposition of sin upon an otherwise good heart. The Canaanites were *already* wicked. Their hearts were *already* hard. God's hardening was a judicial act of confirming them in what they already were, removing restraining grace, and allowing their rebellion to reach its full and final expression. **This is not injustice. This is justice in its most precise and appropriate form.**

---

## VII. Application: What Joshua 11:20 Teaches the Believer

### 1. Fear God.
If God hardened the hearts of the Canaanites so that they could not repent, how terrifying is it to trifle with sin. "It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God" (Hebrews 10:31). There comes a point where God gives sinners over to their own depravity (Romans 1:24, 26, 28). Beware of presuming upon grace.

### 2. Marvel at Mercy.
If you are a believer, you were no better than a Canaanite. You were dead in trespasses and sins. You were a child of wrath (Ephesians 2:1–3). The fact that God softened your heart rather than hardening it is pure, unmerited, sovereign grace. You did not choose God; He chose you (John 15:16). You did not open your own heart; He opened it (Acts 16:14). Worship Him.

### 3. Trust God's Sovereignty in Judgment.
When we see wickedness flourishing in the world, we must trust that God's purposes are being accomplished. He is either extending patience that will lead to repentance, or He is hardening hearts for judgment. Both serve His glory. Both are under His control. We need not wring our hands as though the wicked have escaped His notice.

### 4. Submit to God's Word Without Apology.
Joshua 11:20 is in the Bible because God put it there. It is breathed out by the same Holy Spirit who inspired John 3:16. We do not get to accept the verses that make us comfortable and reject the ones that disturb us. **A domesticated God who never hardens, never judges, and never destroys is an idol — not the God of Scripture.**

---

## Conclusion: The God of Joshua 11:20 Is the God of the Gospel

The same God who hardened the hearts of the Canaanites so that they might be utterly destroyed is the God who sent His Son to die for sinners. These are not contradictions. They are complementary revelations of the same infinitely glorious Being.

At the cross, we see both realities converging: God's full, unmitigated wrath poured out upon sin — and God's full, unmerited mercy extended to sinners. Jesus Christ bore the *cherem* — the total destruction, the utter devotion to wrath — that every sinner deserves. And those whom God has chosen to receive mercy are saved *through* that judgment, not *apart from* it.

The Canaanites received justice. Rahab received grace. Both display the glory of God. Both are good. Both are right.

> *"The LORD is righteous in all his ways, and holy in all his works."* — Psalm 145:17

Let the redeemed of the LORD say so. And let every creature bow before the One who has mercy on whom He will have mercy, and hardens whom He will.

**Soli Deo Gloria.**

---

*"For of him, and through him, and to him, are all things: to whom be glory for ever. Amen."* — Romans 11:36

# Bible Study: The Eternal Torment of the Wicked
## Revelation 14:9-11

---

## Opening Prayer

Ask God to open hearts and minds to receive His Word with reverence, humility, and sober clarity, even when the truths are difficult.

---

## The Text

> **Revelation 14:9-11 (KJV)**
> *"And the third angel followed them, saying with a loud voice, If any man worship the beast and his image, and receive his mark in his forehead, or in his hand, the same shall drink of the wine of the wrath of God, which is poured out without mixture into the cup of his indignation; and he shall be tormented with fire and brimstone in the presence of the holy Lamb, and in the presence of the holy angels: and the smoke of their torment ascendeth up for ever and ever: and they have no rest day nor night, who worship the beast and his image, and whosoever receiveth the mark of his name."*

---

## I. Context of the Passage

### A. The Setting in Revelation

Revelation 14 presents a series of angelic proclamations. Three angels deliver three messages of ultimate urgency:

- **First Angel (v. 6-7):** Proclaims the everlasting gospel — "Fear God, and give glory to him."
- **Second Angel (v. 8):** Announces the fall of Babylon.
- **Third Angel (v. 9-11):** Declares the final and eternal consequences for those who align with the beast.

This third angel's message serves as the most solemn warning in all of Scripture. It is God's final, merciful alarm before judgment falls.

### B. The Broader Biblical Context

This passage does not stand alone. It is the culmination of a consistent biblical teaching about the fate of the unrepentant wicked that stretches from the Old Testament through the words of Christ Himself and into the apostolic writings.

**Discussion Question:** *Why do you think God places this warning in the context of angelic proclamation? What does the urgency of heavenly messengers tell us about the gravity of this truth?*

---

## II. Verse-by-Verse Examination

### A. Verse 9 — The Sin Described

> *"If any man worship the beast and his image, and receive his mark in his forehead, or in his hand..."*

The sin here is ultimate allegiance to that which opposes God. While the immediate context addresses the beast of the end times, the principle extends to all who reject the Lordship of Christ and give their worship to anything or anyone other than God.

**Key Principle:** Worship is the central issue of human existence. Every person will ultimately worship God or something in place of God. The consequences follow accordingly.

**Cross-references:**
- Matthew 6:24 — "No man can serve two masters."
- Romans 1:25 — Those who "worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator."

---

### B. Verse 10a — The Wrath Described

> *"The same shall drink of the wine of the wrath of God, which is poured out without mixture into the cup of his indignation..."*

#### "The wine of the wrath of God"

Scripture consistently uses the metaphor of a cup of wine to describe God's judgment:

- **Psalm 75:8** — "For in the hand of the LORD there is a cup, and the wine is red; it is full of mixture; and he poureth out of the same: but the dregs thereof, all the wicked of the earth shall wring them out, and drink them."
- **Jeremiah 25:15** — "Take the wine cup of this fury at my hand, and cause all the nations, to whom I send thee, to drink it."
- **Isaiah 51:17** — "Awake, awake, stand up, O Jerusalem, which hast drunk at the hand of the LORD the cup of his fury."

#### "Without mixture"

This is a critical phrase. In the ancient world, wine was commonly diluted with water to temper its strength. The phrase **"without mixture"** (Greek: *akratos*) means **undiluted, full strength, unmixed with mercy.**

In this present age, God's judgments are always tempered with mercy. Even in discipline, there is grace. But in the final judgment, the cup will be **pure, unmitigated wrath** — justice without any admixture of mercy.

**Key Theological Point:** God is not only a God of love; He is a God of holy justice. His wrath is not arbitrary or cruel — it is the righteous response of an infinitely holy Being against sin. As R.C. Sproul noted, the wonder is not that God punishes sin, but that He ever shows mercy at all.

**Cross-reference:**
- Nahum 1:2-3 — "God is jealous, and the LORD revengeth... the LORD will not at all acquit the wicked."
- Romans 2:5 — "But after thy hardness and impenitent heart treasurest up unto thyself wrath against the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God."

**Discussion Question:** *What does it mean that God's wrath will be "without mixture"? How does this differ from His judgments in the present age?*

---

### C. Verse 10b — The Nature of the Torment

> *"...and he shall be tormented with fire and brimstone in the presence of the holy Lamb, and in the presence of the holy angels."*

#### "Tormented with fire and brimstone"

Fire and brimstone (sulfur) appear throughout Scripture as instruments of divine judgment:

- **Genesis 19:24** — Sodom and Gomorrah destroyed by fire and brimstone.
- **Isaiah 30:33** — "The pile thereof is fire and much wood; the breath of the LORD, like a stream of brimstone, doth kindle it."
- **Revelation 20:10** — "The devil that deceived them was cast into the lake of fire and brimstone... tormented day and night for ever and ever."
- **Revelation 21:8** — "The fearful, and unbelieving... shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone: which is the second death."

The word **"tormented"** (Greek: *basanizō*) means to test by the touchstone, to torture, to vex with grievous pains. It implies **conscious suffering**, not annihilation. One cannot torment something that has ceased to exist.

#### "In the presence of the holy Lamb and the holy angels"

This is a startling and sobering detail. The torment is not hidden from Christ — it occurs **before Him**. This demolishes any notion that hell is merely "separation from God" in the sense of God being absent. Rather, it is the experience of God's **holy wrath** in His very presence. The same presence that is infinite comfort to the redeemed is infinite terror to the damned.

**Cross-references:**
- 2 Thessalonians 1:9 — "Who shall be punished with everlasting destruction from the presence of the Lord, and from the glory of his power." (Note: "from the presence" can also be rendered "from the face of," indicating it proceeds *from* His presence.)
- Psalm 139:7-8 — "Whither shall I flee from thy presence? ...If I make my bed in hell, behold, thou art there."

**Discussion Question:** *Why is it significant that the torment takes place "in the presence of the holy Lamb"? What does this teach us about the nature of hell?*

---

### D. Verse 11a — The Duration of the Torment

> *"And the smoke of their torment ascendeth up for ever and ever..."*

This is the central clause for the doctrine of eternal punishment.

#### "For ever and ever" (Greek: *eis aiōnas aiōnōn*)

The Greek phrase *eis tous aiōnas tōn aiōnōn* literally means **"unto the ages of the ages."** This is the strongest expression for eternity available in the Greek language. It is critical to note that **this exact same phrase** is used elsewhere in the New Testament to describe:

| Reference | Subject | Duration |
|---|---|---|
| Revelation 4:9-10 | God's existence | *"who liveth for ever and ever"* |
| Revelation 10:6 | God's existence | *"who liveth for ever and ever"* |
| Revelation 11:15 | Christ's reign | *"he shall reign for ever and ever"* |
| Galatians 1:5 | Glory to God | *"to whom be glory for ever and ever"* |
| Revelation 14:11 | Torment of the wicked | *"the smoke of their torment ascendeth up for ever and ever"* |
| Revelation 20:10 | Torment of the devil, beast, and false prophet | *"tormented day and night for ever and ever"* |

**Key Argument:** If *eis tous aiōnas tōn aiōnōn* means something less than eternal in Revelation 14:11, then by the same linguistic logic, God does not live eternally, and Christ's kingdom will end. The phrase **must mean the same thing in every instance.** To limit it in one place is to undermine it everywhere.

**Cross-references on eternal punishment:**
- **Matthew 25:41** — "Depart from me, ye cursed, into **everlasting fire**, prepared for the devil and his angels."
- **Matthew 25:46** — "And these shall go away into **everlasting punishment**: but the righteous into **life eternal**." (Note: The same Greek word *aiōnios* is used for both the punishment and the life. If the life is eternal, so is the punishment.)
- **Mark 9:43-48** — Jesus speaks of hell as a place "where **their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.**" (Quoting Isaiah 66:24)
- **Daniel 12:2** — "And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to **shame and everlasting contempt.**"
- **Jude 7** — Sodom and Gomorrah are set forth as "an example, suffering the vengeance of **eternal fire.**"
- **2 Thessalonians 1:9** — "Who shall be punished with **everlasting destruction** from the presence of the Lord."

**Discussion Question:** *How does the parallel use of "for ever and ever" to describe both God's eternal existence and the torment of the wicked strengthen the case for eternal punishment?*

---

### E. Verse 11b — The Absence of Relief

> *"...and they have no rest day nor night, who worship the beast and his image, and whosoever receiveth the mark of his name."*

#### "No rest day nor night"

This phrase eliminates any hope of intermission, relief, cessation, unconsciousness, or annihilation. The torment is:

1. **Continuous** — "day nor night" indicates unbroken, unceasing suffering.
2. **Conscious** — "no rest" implies awareness. One who does not exist cannot be said to lack rest. Rest is something a conscious being experiences or is denied.
3. **Without relief** — There is no pause, no reprieve, no sleep, no moment of comfort.

Note the devastating contrast with the righteous. In Revelation 14:13, just two verses later:

> *"Blessed are the dead which die in the Lord from henceforth: Yea, saith the Spirit, that they may **rest** from their labours."*

The righteous receive **eternal rest**. The wicked receive **no rest — ever.** The juxtaposition is intentional and deeply sobering.

**Cross-references:**
- **Revelation 20:10** — "And shall be **tormented day and night for ever and ever.**"
- **Luke 16:23-24** — The rich man in Hades: "And in hell he lift up his eyes, being **in torments**... I am **tormented** in this flame." (He is conscious, he remembers, he feels, he speaks, he desires relief.)
- **Luke 16:26** — "And beside all this, between us and you there is **a great gulf fixed**: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot; neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence." (There is no crossing over, no second chance, no escape.)
- **Matthew 13:42** — "And shall cast them into a furnace of fire: there shall be **wailing and gnashing of teeth.**" (Conscious expressions of anguish.)
- **Isaiah 66:24** — "Their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched."

**Discussion Question:** *What is the significance of the contrast between "no rest" for the wicked (v. 11) and "rest" for the righteous (v. 13)?*

---

## III. Addressing Common Objections

### Objection 1: "A loving God would not punish people forever."

**Response:** This objection underestimates the holiness of God, the gravity of sin, and the glory of the One who is offended. Sin against an infinitely holy God is an infinite offense. Jonathan Edwards argued that because God's glory and worthiness are infinite, rejection of Him deserves infinite punishment. Furthermore, this passage itself — and the words of Jesus in the Gospels — plainly teach eternal punishment. We must not edit God's Word to suit our sensibilities.

- **Romans 9:22** — "What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known, endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath fitted to destruction?"
- **Romans 11:22** — "Behold therefore the goodness **and severity** of God."

### Objection 2: "The wicked will be annihilated, not eternally tormented."

**Response:** Annihilationism (or "conditional immortality") cannot account for the language of this passage:

1. **"Tormented"** requires a conscious subject.
2. **"No rest day nor night"** implies ongoing conscious experience.
3. **"For ever and ever"** uses the strongest possible term for unending duration.
4. **"The smoke ascendeth"** — the ongoing ascending of smoke implies an ongoing source of burning, not a past event whose smoke merely lingers.
5. **Revelation 20:10** makes it undeniable — the devil, beast, and false prophet are tormented "day and night for ever and ever." Those cast into the same lake of fire (Revelation 20:15) share the same fate.

### Objection 3: "This is symbolic language and should not be taken literally."

**Response:** Even if one grants that "fire and brimstone" contain symbolic elements (as is possible in apocalyptic literature), symbols represent **realities.** If the symbol is fire, the reality it represents is *at least as terrible* — likely more so. As Charles Spurgeon said: "Do not begin to tell me that the fire is metaphorical. Who cares for that? If a man were to threaten to give me a metaphorical blow on the head, I should care very little about it; but when the 'blow' is explained to mean a real injury, then I take care not to come near the man. And so the threatened punishment of hell, even if it be only metaphorical, means something so terrible that I dare not despise the warning."

The duration language — "for ever and ever," "no rest day nor night" — is not symbolic but temporal, and it matches the same duration language used for God's own eternal nature.

---

## IV. Theological Significance

### A. The Justice of God Is Vindicated

Eternal punishment demonstrates that God takes sin with ultimate seriousness. A God who did not justly punish evil would not be worthy of worship.

- **Revelation 16:5-7** — "Thou art righteous, O Lord... because thou hast judged thus... Even so, Lord God Almighty, **true and righteous are thy judgments.**"
- **Revelation 19:1-3** — Heaven praises God because "**true and righteous are his judgments**... And her smoke rose up **for ever and ever.**"

### B. The Cross of Christ Is Magnified

The doctrine of eternal punishment magnifies the cross. If hell is not eternal, then what exactly did Christ save us from? The greater the penalty, the greater the Savior. The infinite suffering of the wicked displays what the infinite Son of God endured on the cross to redeem His people. He drank the cup of God's wrath **in our place** (Matthew 26:39, 42).

- **2 Corinthians 5:21** — "For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him."
- **Galatians 3:13** — "Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us."
- **1 Peter 3:18** — "For Christ also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God."

### C. The Urgency of the Gospel Is Established

If the punishment is eternal, then evangelism is not optional — it is the most urgent task in the world. Every soul we encounter is headed for one of two eternal destinies.

- **2 Corinthians 5:11** — "Knowing therefore **the terror of the Lord**, we persuade men."
- **Jude 23** — "And others save with fear, **pulling them out of the fire.**"
- **Ezekiel 33:11** — "Say unto them, As I live, saith the Lord GOD, **I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked**; but that the wicked turn from his way and live: **turn ye, turn ye** from your evil ways; for why will ye die?"

### D. The Blessedness of Salvation Is Amplified

We cannot truly appreciate what we have been saved **to** unless we understand what we have been saved **from.** The doctrine of eternal punishment causes the redeemed to worship with greater depth, gratitude, and wonder.

- **Luke 7:47** — "Her sins, which are many, are forgiven; for she loved much: but to whom little is forgiven, the same loveth little."

---

## V. Testimony of the Historic Church

The doctrine of eternal conscious torment has been the consistent teaching of the Christian church throughout its history:

- **The Apostles' Creed and Athanasian Creed** affirm everlasting punishment.
- **Augustine** (354-430): "To say that life eternal shall be endless but punishment eternal shall come to an end is the height of absurdity."
- **Thomas Aquinas** (1225-1274): Affirmed eternal punishment as a matter of divine justice.
- **The Westminster Confession of Faith** (1646), Chapter 33: The wicked shall be "cast into eternal torments."
- **The Second London Baptist Confession** (1689) teaches the same.
- **Charles Spurgeon**: "In hell there is no hope. They have not even the hope of dying — the hope of being annihilated. They are forever, forever, forever lost."
- **Jonathan Edwards**: "The wrath of Almighty God is now undoubtedly hanging over a great part of this congregation. Let every one fly out of Sodom."

---

## VI. Application

### 1. **Examine Yourself**
- 2 Corinthians 13:5 — "Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith."
- Are you resting in Christ alone for salvation? Or are you trusting in your own works, goodness, or religious activity?

### 2. **Flee to Christ**
- If you have never repented of your sin and trusted in Jesus Christ, this passage is a warning of infinite urgency. God commands all men everywhere to repent (Acts 17:30). Christ is the only refuge from the wrath to come (1 Thessalonians 1:10).
- John 3:36 — "He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life: and he that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but **the wrath of God abideth on him.**"

### 3. **Worship with Greater Gratitude**
- If you are in Christ, let this truth produce not cold theological abstraction but **overflowing worship.** You deserved this. Christ took it for you. Marvel at the grace.

### 4. **Evangelize with Greater Urgency**
- Do you truly believe what this text says? Then how can you remain silent? Love for your neighbor demands that you warn them and point them to Christ.
- Proverbs 24:11 — "If thou forbear to deliver them that are drawn unto death, and those that are ready to be slain..."

### 5. **Do Not Soften This Doctrine**
- The temptation in our age is to minimize, reinterpret, or ignore this teaching. But faithfulness to God's Word requires us to teach what He has revealed, even when it is difficult. To withhold this warning is not loving — it is the cruelest form of neglect.

---

## Discussion Questions for Group Study

1. How does this passage shape your understanding of God's holiness?
2. Why is it important that we do not separate God's love from His justice?
3. How does the doctrine of eternal punishment magnify the work of Christ on the cross?
4. How should this text affect the way we share the gospel with unbelievers?
5. What is the danger of softening or denying the doctrine of eternal punishment?
6. How does the contrast between verses 11 and 13 ("no rest" vs. "rest") encourage believers?
7. How does this passage motivate you to personal holiness and devotion to Christ?

---

## Closing Prayer

*Almighty God, we tremble before the truth of Your Word. We acknowledge that Your judgments are righteous and true. We thank You that You have not left us without warning, and we thank You infinitely more that You have not left us without a Savior. We praise You for the Lord Jesus Christ, who bore the wrath we deserved so that we might have eternal life. Give us hearts that worship You with greater gratitude, and give us mouths that faithfully proclaim both the terror of Your judgment and the beauty of Your grace. Burden us for the lost. Keep us from softening Your Word. And let us live every day in light of eternity. In Jesus' name, Amen.*

---

## Memory Verse

> **Matthew 25:46** — *"And these shall go away into everlasting punishment: but the righteous into life eternal."*

---

*Soli Deo Gloria*

# A Compassionate Conversation Guide

## Opening with Empathy

**You:** "I appreciate that you see the genuine goodness in your neighbor. I can tell you care about her deeply, and that's actually why I want to talk about this — because I care about her too, and about what Scripture teaches."

---

## Key Points to Share

### 1. Acknowledging Genuine Virtue

**You:** "I'm not saying your neighbor isn't kind, generous, or sincere. She may genuinely be a more disciplined and outwardly moral person than many churchgoers. That's worth respecting."

### 2. The Biblical Standard

**You:** "But the question isn't whether she's *better than average* — it's what God's standard actually is. Isaiah 64:6 says, 'All our righteous acts are like filthy rags.' That's not describing *bad* deeds — it's describing our *best* efforts apart from God."

**You:** "This includes all of us. My good works, your good works, her good works — none of them bridge the gap between a holy God and sinful humanity."

### 3. The Core Issue
